column1: # gold.tsv — direction -> expected seed symbol(s), for prg-bench.sh (CKP-5b).
# WHAT THIS MEASURES
#   prg-seed.sh turns a natural-language DIRECTION into a ranked list of
#   def-anchored candidate SEED symbols.  The `--no-model` (tool) tier returns
#   the whole ranked list; the model tier (prg-llm.sh) picks the best few FROM
#   that list.  This fixture pins, per direction, the symbol(s) a correct seed
#   MUST surface, so prg-bench.sh can score seed quality across models.
# SCORING (see prg-bench.sh)
#   For a given tier/model, run prg-seed.sh <direction> and collect the emitted
#   seed symbols.  A direction PASSES when the emitted set CONTAINS at least one
#   expected symbol (case-insensitive SUBSTRING match — a candidate name that
#   contains the expected symbol counts, e.g. `mockEmitDebugZip` ⊇ `emitDebugZip`,
#   because that candidate still points the dive at the right code).
#     recall    = fraction of directions that passed
#     precision = (for the model tier) expected-hit seeds / total emitted seeds
#   The point of the model tier is HIGHER PRECISION at comparable recall: the
#   tool tier may emit 30 candidates to catch one gold symbol; a good model
#   returns ~1-3 and still contains it.
# CONSTRAINT ON GOLD ROWS (important)
#   The model tier can only PICK FROM the tool candidate list (prg-seed.sh does
#   `grep -Fxf` against candidates).  So every gold row here is chosen such that
#   its expected symbol already appears in the tool tier's top-30 for a TIGHT
#   direction — otherwise both tiers would score 0 and the row would measure
#   nothing.  Directions are deliberately tight (few generic tokens); a generic
#   token like `table` alone floods 493 candidates and buries the target at
#   rank ~312 (that noise case is what the model tier is meant to rescue, but it
#   can't if the target falls outside the candidate window prg-seed emits).
#   Expected symbols are all TOP-LEVEL EXPORTS (function/const/class/…), because
#   prg-seed.sh's DEFRE anchors on those keywords.  Class METHODS (e.g.
#   `hasActiveTurn`, declared `public hasActiveTurn()`) are intentionally NOT in
#   gold — they are out of prg-seed.sh's designed domain (use prg-graph.sh for
#   method resolution; see Recipe F crash-triage).
# FORMAT  (TAB-separated, 2 columns)
#   direction<TAB>expected_seed1|expected_seed2|...
#   '#' comment lines and blank lines are ignored by prg-bench.sh.
# ROOTS
#   prg-bench.sh runs each direction with --root "modules agents" from the REPO
#   ROOT (prg-seed.sh roots are repo-relative; running elsewhere finds nothing).
# --- TIGHT directions (specific token -> ~1 candidate; both tiers precise) ---
getActiveTraceparent
resolveClientModelSelection
buildDebugZipFileName
onSessionClosed
emitDebugZip
parseTableAddress
checkFormulaError
# --- HARD directions (generic token floods candidates; target buried mid-list
#     but INSIDE the top-30 window).  Tool tier emits ~15-30 candidates at low
#     precision; the model tier must PICK the right one -> its precision edge
#     shows up here.  These are the rows that make the benchmark discriminating.
traceparent tracing
debug zip
